findings.description: An AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block, so they are committed to source control, written to Terraform state, and readable by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. If these are live credentials they grant an attacker every permission the key holds.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables holding secret material are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are displayed in cleartext through the console and API to anyone with function read permissions, with no customer-controlled key policy to separate access.
The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or egress boundary, which eases exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.

The assume role policy trusts the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, omitting the standard confused-deputy guard that scopes role assumption to functions in the owning account.
